name: Dunhill Shell Briar Billiard
description: The Shell Briar finish is perhaps Dunhill's greatest contribution to the art of the pipe. Sandblasted to reveal the grain beneath — every ring of the briar laid bare — this billiard shape has been the companion of thinkers, writers, and statesmen for over a century. The vulcanite stem fits the teeth as naturally as a word fits a sentence. Smoke it slowly; it rewards patience above all things.

name: Savinelli Autograph Freehand
description: Savinelli's Autograph series represents the peak of Italian pipe-making craft — each pipe carved by hand by a single artisan who signs the shank. The freehand shape is a collaboration between man and material: the carver follows the grain, and the pipe tells him where to go. No two are alike. Finished in a deep chestnut stain that only deepens with age.

name: Missouri Meerschaum Country Gentleman
description: Mark Twain smoked one. Einstein smoked one. The Missouri Meerschaum corncob pipe is the great democratiser of the tobacco world — it smokes sweet and cool from the very first bowl, it needs no break-in, and it improves with every smoke. The Country Gentleman's long shank keeps the smoke cool. Do not let its modest price fool you; this is one of the finest smoking instruments made.

name: White Meerschaum Sultan Hand-Carved
description: Carved from a single block of white Turkish meerschaum by craftsmen in Eskişehir — the only city on earth where this mineral is still worked by hand. The Sultan shape flares from a narrow base into a wide, generous bowl, carved with a relief of vines and leaves that will slowly disappear beneath a patina of amber gold as the pipe colours with use. Each one is unique; the carver signs the bottom.

name: Château Latoque Estate Billiard
description: From our estate collection — this French billiard was made in Saint-Claude, likely in the late 1970s, judging by the stamping and stem style. Fully reconditioned by our restoration specialist: bowl reamed, stem polished, shank cleaned and deodorised. It smokes ghost-free. The burl grain across the bowl is exceptional. Estate pipes carry history; this one has earned its patina.

name: Peterson System Standard Churchwarden
description: The churchwarden's long stem cools the smoke to the temperature of a gentle summer evening and keeps the bowl at a comfortable distance from the eye — useful, some say, for stargazing or reading. Peterson's System design adds their patented moisture reservoir in the shank, making this among the driest-smoking long pipes available. The P-Lip mouthpiece is an acquired taste that quickly becomes a preference.
